comments.value: The distinction in my feature request compared to others lies in the need for a long-term categorization of specific disliked users into a category similar to a blacklist. It signifies that these users and us have a rather indifferent relationship, and we prefer not to be approached by them unless we initiate contact. Unless we perceive the potential for further development in our relationship, we do not want them to initiate contact. We would manually remove them from the indifferent friends list if we decide that there is potential for mutual growth. In social settings, veteran players have accumulated numerous friends of this nature—added long ago but with no subsequent interaction. Sometimes, these friends visit at inappropriate times, making it inappropriate to remove them. Hence, there is a need for this functionality.

details: In complex social situations, we are reluctant to add some people we don't like as friends. However, due to intricate relationship structures, we cannot proactively remove these friends. As a result, we are forced to set our online status to yellow or red for extended periods. Therefore, we hope to have the ability to individually set the online status for specific friends as yellow or red. Additionally, when in yellow or red status, we wish to have a horizontal menu to choose between absolute "Do Not Disturb" mode or allowing whitelisted users to join without approval, along with determining their display position. To avoid complexity for regular users, we recommend making this feature available in the menu and revealing advanced options for professional users with specific needs。At the same time, we hope that when adding a user as a friend, we can choose the nature of our relationship with them. This would allow us to specify whether we prefer a courteous connection without deeper interaction, a standard friendship, or an advanced friendship.
title: Advanced Online Status Settings
